figures.evidence: Re-derived from the code. Only three CAN transmit call sites exist in firmware/panel and shared: main.c:1663 (exchange()), selftest.c:33 (status request) and :66 (probe). link_host start() refuses while h->pending (link_host.c:36) and the slot clears only after LINK_HOST_TIMEOUT_MS 1000u (link_host.h:29; link_host.c:257-258), so a stall under 1000 ms sees one request's frames at most: LINK_MAX_REGS 32 / LINK_CAN_REGS_PER_FRAME 4 = 8 (link_msg.h:21; link_can.h:69-72). control_pump() talks to nothing on the link (main.c:610-611). Self-test: status tries 50 ms apart (selftest.c:28-43), probes one at a time with a 50 ms timeout (can_selftest.c:142), 20 ms receive plus 2 ms delay after the last probe before the closing status request (selftest.c:57-101, :116), then the identity poll (1 frame) at least 50 ms after the last status try (main.c:1079-1101). 9 frames span 372 ms; 10 need 422 ms. 3 ms holds one self-test frame or the 8 of one write.

figures.evidence: Bit count re-derived: base-format CAN FD frame, 0 data bytes, BRS: SOF 1 + ID 11 + RRS + IDE + FDF + res = 16 nominal bits; BRS, ESI, DLC 4, stuff count 4, CRC 17, 6 fixed stuff bits, CRC delimiter = 34 bits at 5000 kbit/s = 6.8 us; ACK, ACK delimiter, EOF 7, intermission 3 = 12 nominal. 28 + 6.8 = 34.8 us lower bound. floor(400,000/34.8) + 1 = 11,495; floor(3,000/34.8) + 1 = 87. 29-bit FD frame 53.8 us: 7,435 and 56; classic 0-byte base frame 47 bits: 8,511 and 64. CiA page: FDF bit, rate switch at the BRS sample point, 3-bit Gray-coded stuff count with parity and a fixed stuff bit, 17-bit CRC up to 16 bytes. AN5348: data phase ends at the sample point of the CRC delimiter. DroneCAN 4.1: 'DroneCAN uses only CAN 2.0B frame format (29-bit identifiers)' and 'can share the same bus with other protocols based on CAN 2.0A (11-bit identifiers)'.

IOBoard.md:57 'the external CAN transceiver is in standby while the enable is low'; :238 the same; Research.md:280 (R2 row) 'The external port's transceiver has a standby input, held in standby while the enable node is low'; Research.md:590 (V30 question) lists 'the external CAN transceiver's standby' among the gates. Monostable.md:30 at 23c82ca names as gates only the buffer's output enable and the high-side switches on the servo rail and the ESC pack; grep finds no CAN transceiver on that page. figures.figure: re-rank report: CAN controller clock (P3's missed function)
figures.evidence: The conclusion holds: Research.md:28 puts 'crystals and inductors not fixed in round 1' in round 2, and :27 fixes only the RP2354B's crystal; the tolerances are carried as requirements (V26 under +/-5,000 ppm, V27 +/-3,876 ppm). One stated fact does not hold as written: 'For the MCP2518FD it is a 40 or 20 MHz crystal or resonator'. DS20006027B page 1 lists '40, 20 or 4 MHz Crystal or Ceramic Resonator; External Clock Input', and Table 7-6 note 3 limits FSCK to 0.85 x FSYSCLK/2. With a 20 MHz SYSCLK the SPI limit is 8.5 MHz, under the link's 10 MHz (IOBoard.md:170). On the link the clock is therefore 40 MHz, or 4 MHz with the x10 PLL (FDRIFT 10 ppm added), not 20 MHz. The sentence would pass a 20 MHz crystal to round 2 that breaks the link's SPI requirement.

figures.evidence: Every controller line of IOBoard.md is named: :167 bus, :168 exact 1 Mbit/s at 75 %, :169 clock making it, :170 SPI mode 0 at 10 MHz and an active-low interrupt with a pull-up, :171 frames held (V16, Q8 only), :172 error counters, flags and overflow, :174 acknowledging (V28), :175 3.3 V logic, :540/:560 RXCAN and TXCAN test points. Raised by P1 rows naming the function: V16 (Research.md:576), V26 (:586), V28 (:588), each carried at the found value (9 in 400 ms and 8 in 3 ms; under +/-5,000 ppm; about 1000 ms). V7 (:567, one range for the whole board) is carried as 0 to 50 degC. No entry is weaker than its source.

The loop-delay entry is weaker than IOBoard.md:177 sets. It derives 350 ns from 2 x 5 m of cable. IOBoard.md:177 reads 'the bus under 5 m; each board's branch under 30 cm'. The path between the two transceivers is branch + bus + branch, up to 5.6 m. That gives (750 ns - 2 x 5.6 m x 5 ns/m)/2 = 347 ns, with both ends at 75 % (docs/Link.md:198) and the display's transceiver taken as equal (an assumption; the display's transceiver delay is not stated in the tree). The other entries match their sources: :167 classic CAN at 1 Mbit/s, :175 RXD at 3.3 V, V25 5.5 V (Research.md:585), :337-338 rails, V7 0 to 50 degC. No ranked part changes: TCAN3413DR 180 ns, SN65HVD233DR 135 ns and TCAN1044VDRQ1 210 ns all meet 347 ns.

Raised by P1 rows naming the function: V17 (Research.md:577, Q8 only) carried as frames reported against 11,495 and 87; V20 (:580) CAN FD with classic; V27 (:587) +/-3,876 ppm. V21 (named for the transceiver) carried as 1000/5000 kbit/s. IOBoard.md:65 own controller; :175 3.3 V logic; Research.md:359 (P5 row) SPI as the host interface; V7 0 to 50 degC. IOBoard.md sets no other line for the external controller (:170 and :540 belong to the link). No entry is weaker than its source.

The loop-delay entry, 237 ns, is weaker than V22's found value. It is derived at DroneCAN's recommended 87.5 % sample point: (875 - 400)/2. V22 (Research.md:582, found) gives the valid nominal sample point at 1000 kbit/s as 75 % to 90 %. Any remote node on the port may sample at 75 %. Arbitration and ACK against that node need loop(IO board) + loop(remote) + 2 x 40 m x 5 ns/m <= 750 ns. With the remote transceiver taken as equal, as the entry assumes, the limit is (750 - 400)/2 = 175 ns. DroneCAN's 0.3 m stub limit, if counted for both nodes, lowers it about 3 ns more. Against 175 ns, TCAN3413DR (180 ns max, SLLSFS8A 5.9) and TCAN1044VDRQ1 (210 ns) fail. TCAN1042HGVDRQ1 (160/175 ns) and TCAN1472VDRQ1 (155/160 ns) meet it. The other entries match their sources: V18, V19 5 ms, V20/V21, V23 0 V, V24 +30 V, IOBoard.md:175, :192, rails, V7.
